analysis:
Examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head lines 526-1722) and ChatTemplateFixes.swift patch. Changed behavior: (1) in the engine-v2 vision path (lines 714-724, 747-749) the prompt-side reasoning prefix is now computed from the rendered media prompt tokens and passed as stopStringScope into bridge.submitTokenized, so stop strings are scoped to the content channel as they are on the text path (line 975). (2) The previously later-computed reasoningPrefix is removed and the same value is reused when building the event stream (line 771). (3) ChatTemplateFixes adds a GPT-OSS stopStringScope helper plus an MLXLMCommon import, with no visible caller in the supplied units.

Security view: this is a correctness and parsing change on the provider-local inference path (TB-007). It adds no new network surface, key handling, attestation, or authorization logic. The cache controls are unchanged. cacheScope and cacheEnabled are still passed through (lines 736-737, 970-971), and the media-token path in prepareNativeMiMoMedia still sets cacheEnabled:false (line 1105). T-041 cache scoping, TTL, and HMAC posture are untouched. Reservation release and cancellation paths are unchanged: the catch block at lines 783-816 still releases the media gate and releaseBox. The reasoningPrefix computation runs inside the do block, so a throw there is also covered by those releases. The decodeTail closure only decodes prompt tokens that are already in memory. No plaintext leakage or fail-open behavior was introduced.

Remaining unverified: the implementations of ReasoningStopScope.scope, GPTOSSHarmonyTemplateFix.finalChannelStopScope, and the bridge's stopStringScope handling are outside the supplied evidence. I could not confirm that a wrong scope cannot let a stop sequence be missed or suppress reasoning leakage. That is a functional concern rather than a demonstrated security regression.
